sections.content:
29,945 people

were counted on the census as "insurance underwriters" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Insurance underwriters identify and measure the risks associated with an activity, determine whether this risk is insurable and issue insurance policies which provide financial compensation in the event of loss.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "insurance underwriters", 17.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "insurance underwriters" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "insurance underwriters" included:

  • customer service supervisors
  • primary education teaching professionals
  • natural and social science professionals (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "insurance underwriters" there were a similar number of men and women (49.9% compared with 50.1%).

This means "insurance underwriters" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 49.9% and women made up 50.1% of "insurance underwriters"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "insurance underwriters" included:

  • other researchers, unspecified discipline
  • database administrators and web content technicians
  • advertising accounts managers and creative directors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "insurance underwriters" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "insurance underwriters" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "insurance underwriters", 6.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (87.6% compared with 12.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (99%) than self-employed (1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
